newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic power rises on transmission limits.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic power rises on transmission limits.

text.p: Day-ahead bulk prices in the Mid-Atlantic electricity market rose Monday on transmission limits in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool, which began last week, market sources said.
Transmission restrictions were triggered by high import demand from eastern PJM for cheaper generation from the west.

A refueling outage at the 1,055 megawatt (MW) Limerick 2 nuclear unit in Pennsylvania further cut power flows eastward, forcing utilities to switch on expensive oil and natural gas generation to balance the grid if they should need to bring cheap, coal-fired power from the west.

Dispatch rates for peak power Tuesday in the eastern half of PJM edged up 50 cents to $37.50 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Friday's level. Tuesday's production costs in western PJM increased to $18.00 from Friday's $16.00, market sources said.
Firm, peak PJM electricity for Tuesday (excluding transmission costs) climbed to $25.50-26.25/MWh from Friday's $24.50-25.50 for delivery today.
PJM power prices for firm, off-peak delivery Tuesday remained in the $16.00-17.00 range.
Forecasts showed temperatures averaging near normal through mid-week with daytime readings peaking in the 30-40 degrees F range. Some rain or snow is possible in the region Thursday night or Friday.
Most deferred PJM values were flat to lower in line with corresponding forward deliveries in the natural gas market, market sources said.
Swing natural gas prices at the Philadelphia city gate was notionally assessed at $2.75-3.00 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), compared with Friday's $2.85-2.95.
As of 1300 EST, NYMEX March Henry Hub gas futures were nearly unchanged from Friday's close at $2.190/mmBtu.
PJM power deliveries until end of February slipped to $26.00-27.00 from $26.75-27.25 Friday.
March PJM power prices softened to $23.80-24.00 from Friday's quote of $23.90-24.10.
PJM prices for April and May narrowed to $21.90-22.00 from $21.90-22.15 Friday while June PJM power held at $24.75-25.00.
July/August PJM power fell to $29.80-30.00 from Friday's $30.00-30.20.
PJM third-quarter quotes tightened to $27.80-28.00 from $27.80-28.10 Friday, and fourth-quarter PJM prices remained at $23.85-24.00. Firm, peak PJM deliveries for 1998 was still valued near $25.95.
Separately, a 600 MW Homer City, Pa., coal-fired unit is expected to resume operation later today after being taken off line last Thursday to repair a flame scanner.
